fatal_errors: The proposed method is spark plasma sintering, whereas the target method is liquid-metal dealloying of a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu.
The hypothesis replaces the target as-cast dendrite/interdendrite precursor with an unsupported generic RHEA–Cu powder mixture.
The claimed mechanism of kinetically suppressing segregation does not reconstruct the selective Ti–Cu exchange, retention of W/Ta/V-rich ligaments, or formation of a W-rich passivating interlayer.
Neither cited source demonstrates SPS processing of an RHEA–Cu composite or supports overcoming positive RHEA–Cu mixing enthalpy by rapid consolidation.
The predicted mechanical and irradiation improvements are not supported by the cited evidence and omit the target thermal-conductivity outcome.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad challenge of combining Cu with refractory alloys, but otherwise diverges from the target. The reported solution relies on liquid-metal dealloying at 1200 °C for 96 h, using Ti/V-rich interdendritic channels as sacrificial regions to produce aligned Cu channels and continuous RHEA ligaments. Stability arises from selective Ti extraction and an approximately 300 nm W-rich interfacial layer, not from suppressing diffusion during SPS. The proposed comparison against conventional sintering is a reasonable generic falsification test for the SPS hypothesis, but it does not test selective replacement, interfacial passivation, directional bicontinuity, or the key temperature-dependent thermal performance. The evidence only supports general RHEA properties and SPS fabrication of a Cu-free RHEA, so it cannot validate the central intervention or mechanism.
